Vertex: A point where two or more constraint boundaries intersect in the feasible region of a linear programming problem.  In the Simplex method, optimal solutions are found at vertices.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 5><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 16><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 29>

Basic Variable: In the Simplex method, a variable that is expressed in terms of non-basic variables in a dictionary. Non-basic Variable: In the Simplex method, a variable that is set to zero in a given iteration of the algorithm.  The values of the basic variables are determined by the values of the non-basic variables.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 14><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 15><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 26><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28>

Pivot Operation: The process of exchanging a basic and a non-basic variable in the Simplex method to move from one vertex to another in the feasible region.<L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 27><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 28>

Dictionary: A representation of a linear programming problem where the basic variables are expressed as functions of the non-basic variables. Largest-Increase Rule: A pivot rule in the simplex method that selects the entering variable that produces the largest increase in the objective function value.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 6><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 7><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 8>

Klee-Minty Example: A worst-case example for the simplex method, demonstrating exponential time complexity for certain pivot rules.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 2><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 3><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 4><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 5>

Bland's Rule: A pivot rule in the simplex method designed to avoid cycling, but not necessarily to improve efficiency.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>

Lexicographic Method: A method for choosing the leaving variable in the simplex method to prevent cycling.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>

Smoothed Complexity: A measure of the complexity of an algorithm that considers the effect of small random perturbations to the input data.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 11>

Interior Method: A class of algorithms for linear programming that traverse the interior of the feasible region, in contrast to the simplex method which follows the boundary.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 12>

Algorithm Solutions:
Simplex Method: Iteratively move from one vertex of the feasible region to another by setting non-basic variables to zero and choosing a new set of (non)basic variables to improve the objective function.  This is equivalent to moving from vertex to vertex in the feasible region. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 6>

Pivot Operation: Interchange one basic and one non-basic variable in the dictionary by rewriting the equations to express the basic variables in terms of the non-basic variables and updating the objective function accordingly. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 9><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 10><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 12><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 13><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 14><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 15>

Auxiliary Problem: Introduce a new variable  $x_0$ and modify the constraints to create a new problem whose feasible region includes the origin. Solve this problem to find a feasible solution for the original problem. <L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 32><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 33><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 34><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 35><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 36><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 37><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 38><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 39><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 40><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 41><L[2024-08-27-ExSimplex] 42>

Klee-Minty Example:  Maximize $\sum_{j=1}^{n} 2^{n-j} x_j$ subject to $\sum_{j=1}^{n} 2^{i-j} x_j + x_i \le 100^{i-1}$, $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$, and $x_j \ge 0$, $j = 1, 2, \dots, n$.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 2><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 3>

Largest-Coefficient Rule:  Select the non-basic variable with the largest coefficient in the objective function row of the dictionary to enter the basis.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 4><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 5><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 6>

Largest-Increase Rule: Select the non-basic variable whose entrance into the basis yields the largest increase in the objective function value.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 6><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 7><L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 8>

Bland's Rule: Choose the entering variable with the smallest index among those with positive reduced costs.  Choose the leaving variable with the smallest index among those that satisfy the minimum ratio test.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>

Randomized Pivot Rule: Randomly permute the indices of the variables; then use Bland's rule for entering variables and the lexicographic method for leaving variables.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 10>

Interior Method:  This algorithm traverses the interior of the feasible region to find the optimal solution, unlike the Simplex method which follows the boundary.<L[2024-09-05-SimplexEfficiency] 12>
